The tallest mountain in the world is Mount Everest, measured by its peak altitude above sea level. 
Core Facts
  • Height: 8,848.86 meters (29,031.7 feet).
  • Location: The Himalayas, on the border between Nepal and China. 
Alternative Measurements
Depending on how you measure a mountain, two other peaks can claim this title: 
  • Mauna Kea (Tallest from Base): This inactive volcano in Hawaii measures over 10,210 meters (33,500 feet) from its underwater base to its peak. Only 4,207 meters (13,803 feet) rise above sea level. 
  • Mount Chimborazo (Closest to Space): Located in Ecuador, its peak is the farthest point from the center of the Earth. This happens because the Earth bulges at the equator, pushing this mountain higher into the atmosphere than Everest despite its lower official altitude of 6,263 meters (20,548 feet).
